nodes.label: Question, specimen and controls
nodes.summary: Start with the biological question and specimen. These choices constrain which viral fractions can be recovered and what a negative result can mean.
nodes.why_it_matters: The observed virome reflects both biology and technical selection across collection, enrichment, extraction and sequencing.
nodes.outputs: A defined target, specimen context, controls and sequencing strategy.
nodes.caveat: A method-negative result does not establish biological absence when the target fraction may not have been recovered or the assay lacks sensitivity.

nodes.label: Recovery and sequencing strategy
nodes.summary: Choose total metagenomics, particle enrichment, metatranscriptomics, capture, or read-length strategy to match the target and specimen.
nodes.why_it_matters: Enrichment, extraction and library preparation preferentially recover or exclude viral fractions; sequencing strategy is part of the measurement, not a neutral prelude.
nodes.outputs: A documented laboratory protocol, expected viral fraction, read type and control plan.
nodes.caveat: No single strategy captures all DNA and RNA viruses, intracellular and extracellular particles, or integrated elements equally well.

nodes.label: Read quality control
nodes.summary: Inspect raw reads, adapters, base quality, duplicates and library-specific artifacts; retain an auditable record of filtering.
nodes.why_it_matters: Low-quality or artifactual reads can increase computational load and contribute misleading taxonomic matches.
nodes.outputs: Quality reports and documented raw-to-filtered read counts, with unfiltered data retained when permitted.
nodes.caveat: Aggressive trimming or filtering can remove real viral signal. Apply thresholds consistently and report versions and parameters.

nodes.label: Human-read removal
nodes.summary: Screen reads against an appropriate human reference when required for privacy, downstream efficiency or study design.
nodes.why_it_matters: Reference choice, alignment settings and filtering policy change retained reads and can affect both privacy risk and viral recovery.
nodes.outputs: Filtered reads, screening logs, reference/version details, and counts before and after removal.
nodes.caveat: Host-like viral sequences may be removed, and residual human sequence may remain. Filtering is not itself proof of privacy or biological neutrality.

links.label: Human-read removal tools in the methods matrix

nodes.label: K-mer and profile-based screening
nodes.summary: Classify reads or estimate profiles against reference databases using k-mers, coverage filters or combined nucleotide and translated searches.
nodes.why_it_matters: Read-based screening can detect low-abundance, reference-represented viruses even when reads do not assemble into contigs.
nodes.outputs: Candidate taxonomic assignments or abundance profiles, together with the database, confidence and coverage metrics.
nodes.caveat: Reference composition limits discovery. A few matching reads or an abundance estimate alone does not confirm a virus, recover a genome or establish infection.

links.label: Read-based profiling tools in the methods matrix

nodes.label: Reference mapping and recruitment
nodes.summary: Recruit reads to candidate reference genomes or contigs, then inspect identity, breadth, depth, paired-read consistency and competing matches.
nodes.why_it_matters: The mapping database and alignment thresholds determine which reads count as supporting a candidate and how abundance is estimated.
nodes.outputs: Per-reference alignments, coverage breadth/depth and candidate-specific supporting-read evidence.
nodes.caveat: A local match or narrow conserved region can be misleading. Competitive references, coverage distribution, controls and ambiguity from multi-mapping reads matter.

nodes.label: Abundance and comparison
nodes.summary: Estimate read support and compare samples only after defining normalization, multi-mapping policy, controls and the unit of analysis.
nodes.why_it_matters: Mapping stringency, genome length normalization and ambiguous reads can materially change abundance estimates and cross-sample conclusions.
nodes.outputs: A reproducible abundance table with normalization, denominator, database version and uncertainty/controls described.
nodes.caveat: Relative abundance is not absolute viral load. Sequencing depth, enrichment efficiency, batch effects and contamination can mimic biological differences.

nodes.label: De novo assembly
nodes.summary: Assemble quality-controlled reads into contigs to support candidate discovery and genome-level analysis.
nodes.why_it_matters: Assembly provides sequence context beyond individual reads, but its yield depends on coverage, strain diversity, repeats and read technology.
nodes.outputs: Contigs or assembled genomes plus assembly statistics, graph/read support and reproducible settings.
nodes.caveat: Assembly alone does not prove a contig is viral, complete or non-chimeric. Preserve graph and read-level evidence for candidate review.

links.label: Assembly tools in the methods matrix

nodes.label: Viral-sequence identification
nodes.summary: Assess contigs with complementary homology, hallmark-marker, sequence-composition and machine-learning evidence; combine signals where possible.
nodes.why_it_matters: Each evidence class has different strengths. Current tools often combine them, and tool choice changes which candidates enter the observed virome.
nodes.outputs: Candidate viral contigs with per-tool scores, supporting genes/alignments and method-specific uncertainty.
nodes.caveat: No classifier score alone establishes a novel virus. Short contigs, plasmids, cellular sequences, database gaps and assembly artifacts can produce uncertain calls.

links.label: Viral-sequence identification tools in the methods matrix

nodes.label: Genome quality and similarity
nodes.summary: Assess completeness, contamination, read support and possible provirus boundaries; compare sufficiently supported genomes with explicit identity and coverage metrics.
nodes.why_it_matters: Quality thresholds and genome-similarity rules affect which sequences are retained, dereplicated and interpreted as distinct.
nodes.outputs: Quality estimates, boundary calls, pairwise similarity/ANI and clustering results with database and threshold versions.
nodes.caveat: ANI is a genome/contig comparison concept, not read classification. Incomplete genomes, alignment fraction and reference coverage affect similarity; a cluster is not automatically a formal taxon.

links.label: Genome quality and clustering tools in the methods matrix

nodes.label: Taxonomy and genome context
nodes.summary: Assign taxonomy using sequence similarity, genome-wide relationships, hallmark genes and curated taxonomic references appropriate to the viral group.
nodes.why_it_matters: Taxonomic resolution depends on reference diversity, genome completeness and the classification system; methods may disagree or stop above species level.
nodes.outputs: Taxonomic assignments and their supporting identity, coverage, gene-content or genome-context evidence.
nodes.caveat: Do not equate one nearest database match or clustering threshold with a formally established species or biological equivalence.

nodes.label: Host and functional hypotheses
nodes.summary: Predict virus–host links and annotate genes with sequence, marker, structure or model-based evidence; prioritize consequential claims for orthogonal validation.
nodes.why_it_matters: Host predictions and viral protein annotations extend interpretation beyond sequence detection, but each depends on reference coverage, model domain and contextual evidence.
nodes.outputs: Host-link predictions, gene annotations and structure/function hypotheses with confidence, evidence source and database/model versions.
nodes.caveat: Predictions do not prove infection, host range, activity or experimentally validated function. Structure similarity (including Foldseek) and predicted structure (including AlphaFold) generate hypotheses, not functional confirmation.

links.label: Host and functional interpretation tools in the methods matrix

nodes.label: Validation and reporting
nodes.summary: Use negative and positive controls, quantitative standards and orthogonal evidence to evaluate key findings; report enough detail for reproducibility.
nodes.why_it_matters: Low-biomass contamination, database versions and undocumented thresholds can otherwise be mistaken for biological signal or prevent cross-study comparison.
nodes.outputs: Validated or explicitly provisional claims; controls; parameters; software/database versions; and traceable intermediate results.
nodes.caveat: Keep claim strength proportional to the evidence: detection, genome recovery, activity, host linkage and function are distinct conclusions.
